result.note: Tests a central law limiting state mineral taxation, its treatment of past levies, and its link to a 2024 Supreme Court ruling.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, President Droupadi Murmu granted assent to the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026. Consider the following statements about the Act:
items: It bars states from imposing taxes, cesses or other levies on mineral rights and mineral bearing land except under conditions set by the Centre.
States must refund levies on mineral rights that they had already received before the law took effect.
It overturns a 2024 Supreme Court ruling that let states tax mineral rights.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong: payments already received by states will not be refunded, though levies not collected before the law takes effect become invalid. The Act reverses the 2024 Supreme Court ruling and restores the Centre's control over levies on mineral rights.
questions.source: Levies not collected before the law takes effect will become invalid, while payments already received by states will not be refunded.
